# neuron v0.1.4

Windows 10/11 (x86_64). The installer and portable ZIP include the tray app and CLI. The binaries are unsigned. Verify downloads with `SHA256SUMS.txt`; `SOURCE.txt` records the source commit and build method.

More intentional UI across the board, general controllers, a little wildlife on your keyboard, and more things to bind. Lots of pen testing happened along the way, and lots of bugs were fixed as a result. neuron is starting to feel like a *real* product 😳

![Wildlife: neuron's software lighting rendered on a mock keyboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worflor/neuron/v0.1.4/docs/media/release-v0.1.4-wildlife.webp)

## More intentional UI

The action palette now has a group rail: narrow the choices, find what you want, and configure it right there. Direct binds are more compact, filtering keeps the right binding attached to its editor, and device identity lives in the lighting preview's bezel. More of the interface answers the next question where you're already looking.

## NOW SUPPORTS: general controllers

![Controller binds and device badges in neuron's editor (demo state)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worflor/neuron/v0.1.4/docs/media/release-v0.1.4-controllers.webp)

Buttons, sticks, triggers and hats can all become binds. Hold a cast trigger and aim the radial with a stick; on the verified Xbox-protocol pad, the wheel has feel too, with detents, clicks and a little kick when you fire.

General pads are step one toward the devices I want neuron to work with. I don't own a Razer Tartarus V2 to test yet. Switch Pro is in sight, but Nintendo has some black magic I have to understand how to cast first.

Tested on a PowerA pad on Windows.

## Lighting updates across the *board*... heh, get it?

**New highlight: Wildlife.** A little seasonal cellular habitat on your keys. Colonies grow, move and fade through spring, summer, autumn and winter, and your typing shapes what happens around them. Leave it alone and it keeps living: quiet habitats can recover instead of settling into an empty board. Speed and density let you tune the activity, and the habitat respects the region you give it.

![Wildlife in motion: source lighting rendered on a mock keyboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worflor/neuron/v0.1.4/docs/media/release-v0.1.4-wildlife-motion.webp)

[Watch the full seasonal cycle](https://github.com/worflor/neuron/releases/download/v0.1.4/neuron-v0.1.4-wildlife.mp4). Production lighting code, simulated typing, rendered keyboard.

The other effects got attention too: Fire gains drifting wind, Starlight gets shaped twinkles and a little shimmer, Reactive and Ripple respond to holding and releasing keys, and Typing Heat builds while you hold. Saved lighting effects also survive editing more reliably.

## New actions!!

- **Clipboard transforms.** Clean up text, change case, sort or deduplicate lines, format JSON, convert CSV, encode/decode, or replace text with regex. Chain operations and preview the result; a stored Python macro can also be a transform step :)
- **Clipboard history.** Restore a previous clipboard snapshot from this session. Existing Pockets gained fuller format preservation and more reliable restoration.
- **Screenshots.** Capture the screen, the foreground window, or a selected region to the clipboard, a PNG, or both. Region selection needs the resident app.
- **Lighting layers.** Bind toggles, presets, reordering, colours, parameters and regions in the active lighting stack.
- **Undo.** Restore the latest supported audio, profile or lighting change in this session, provided its value hasn't changed since.
- **Dial scrolling.** The existing dial can now scroll the pane under your pointer, or stay anchored to the pane you started on.

Also: Naga side plates have their own identities and steadier swap handling, firmware-backed binds were hardened, and neuron can import the key and mouse-button mappings in a Synapse 3 mapping log.

## Lots of testing, lots of fixes

Pen testing and adversarial tests turned up bugs across clipboard formats, screenshots, nested actions, editor state, controller identity and firmware-backed input. This release fixes those paths and expands the regression coverage around them.

## Before you install

Use the installer for a normal install, or unpack the portable ZIP into a writable folder and run `neuron-app.exe`.

This is still the Windows beta. Tartarus V2 has not been tested (i don't think it'll work *yet*); Switch Pro is not ready. Linux is being worked on but has no release package; Macn't.
